title: Aral Sea: 41 years of shrinking, and today's radar
finding: Open water in the box fell from 46,371.1 km2 (1985) to 9,018.8 km2 (2026), 80.6 % less (Landsat).

sections.what: The Aral Sea shrank as its rivers were diverted to irrigation; the summer Landsat photos show it year by year.
sections.why: The same rivers feed the Fergana valley, so upstream water use reaches all the way here.
sections.radar: On the NISAR pass, calm open water is dark and wet salt crust and rough ground are bright. We show the radar; we do not measure water area from it here.
sections.validation: Water areas are from Landsat (MNDWI > 0 on clear pixels), not from NISAR. Salt flats can look like water to radar, so no radar water number is claimed.
sections.limits: The 1985 frame borrows 44.7 % of its pixels from 1986 (cloud fill). GIBS radar is display-scaled, not calibrated dB.
